Non-Immigrant Visa — O-X (Longstay 5+5 years). Purpose of visit: Long-stay (O-X) for foreigners aged 50 years or older (who wish to stay in Thailand for 5 years + 5 years).
Documents the Thai e-Visa system asks for:
1. Biodata page of Passport or Travel Document
2. Photograph taken within the last six months.
3. Proof of permanent residence in the country where the application is submitted
4. Financial evidence with a fixed deposit of at least 3,000,000 THB or at least 1,800,000 THB together with an income of at least 1,200,000 THB per year in a Thai bank located in Thailand (e.g., bank statements for the last three months, proof of earnings)
5. Medical certificate issued from the country where the application is submitted, showing no prohibitive diseases as indicated in the Ministerial Regulation No.14 (B.E. 2535) (certificate shall be valid for not more than three months)
6. Foreign Insurance Certificate, as stipulated by the Office of Insurance Commission and Health Insurance of Thailand, must be completed, signed, and stamped by the insurance company. The form can be downloaded from https://longstay.tgia.org.
7. Biography
8. Certificate of criminal record clearance from the country of nationality. (In case the applicants have permanent residence in another country, the aforementioned document is required from both the country of nationality and the country of permanent residence.)
9. Health insurance issued by an insurer in Thailand, with an outpatient benefit of at least 40,000 THB and an inpatient benefit of at least 400,000 THB.

metadata.title: Non-Immigrant Visa — O-X (Longstay 5+5 years): Long-stay (O-X) for foreigners aged 50 years or older (who wish to stay in Thailand for 5 years + 5 years)

WHAT IS LTR VISA
Thailand is introducing a new visa called “Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa” which is a program that provides a range of tax and non-tax benefits to enhance the country’s attractiveness as a regional hub for living and doing business for ‘high-potential’ individuals. Today, Thailand is already home to multinational corporations from all over the world and one of the most important tourist destinations in Asia.

Is it possible to submit the LTR Visa application directly to the LTR Visa unit ?
No, the application must be submitted online only through the official website: https://ltr.boi.go.th
What is the application fee for applying for the LTR visa? When is the full payment of 50,000 baht due ?
The application and processing for the LTR visa are free of charge. However, once your application is approved, you will need to make a full payment of 50,000 baht for the issuance of the LTR visa. This payment is due on the appointment date at the Immigration Bureau office located at TIESC in Bangkok.
If I have the LTR visa, do I still need to register for the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) after May 1st when I want to enter Thailand ?
Yes, the TDAC is required for all foreigners entering Thailand starting May 1st, 2025. You will need to register for the TDAC every time you enter Thailand.

If you are still in the process of applying for an LTR visa, do not terminate your current visa beforehand.
What are the choices of payments for LTR Visa processing fee?
Acceptable payment options include Thai mobile banking (QR code scanning and cash only. However, if you choose to issue e-visa abroad, please follow the Royal Thai Consular protocol.
Which type of LTR visa can one apply for a work permit?
Wealthy Global Citizens, Wealthy Pensioners, Highly Skilled Professionals and Dependents types are included, except for those in the Work-from-Thailand Professionals category, as they are required to be remote workers according to our criteria.

In such cases, you may schedule an appointment to consult with us through the Online Clinic. Please contact ltr@boi.go.th or add our official LINE ID: @smartvisathailand to access the appointment booking system.
How should I dress when visiting Thailand Investment and Expat Services Center (TIESC) for LTR Visa issuance or to consult with the officer?
It is advised to dress politely in proper business attire and appropriate shoes. Please note that the immigration or LTR Visa officer reserve the right to refuse service if they deem the clothing to be inappropriate.

Holders of the LTR visa under the Work-from-Thailand category cannot engage in work or activities with Thai employers that generate income in Thailand because this visa does not allow for a work permit. Answer: Residence Certificate is an official one-page document that states you are living in Thailand. A Residence Certificate is a document issued by immigration that confirms where a foreigner resides. This document can be used to obtain a Thai driver's license/ buy a car.
Please be aware that a residence certificate is a letter confirming your address in Thailand that can be obtained from either your home embassy in Thailand or the immigration bureau nearest to your address.
You can actually obtain this document at the immigration residing your residence if you have done a 90-day report from your latest arrival in Thailand.
Please be advised that there are 3 ways to obtain the residence certificate, which are as
follows;
- The embassy of your country in Thailand (Please check with your embassy to see if they are still able to issue this letter as some embassy cannot do that)
- The immigration where you are residing (If you are in Bangkok, you can do it at Immigration Chaeng Wattana; if you are in other provinces, you can do it at the immigration bureau where you live in Thailand.)
